name: Vitality/Energy Monitoring Circuit
short_description: Integrates interoceptive signals, fatigue level, sleep pressure, and metabolic rate to estimate resource availability and regulate activity motivation.

components.name: INTEROCEPTIVE_INTEGRATOR
components.description: Aggregates internal bodily state signals including heart rate, respiration, and visceral cues

components.name: FATIGUE_MONITOR
components.description: Tracks cumulative fatigue and recovery status

components.name: RESOURCE_ESTIMATOR
components.description: Synthesizes interoceptive state, fatigue, and metabolic signals to estimate overall energy resources

key_references: Craig, A. D. (2009). How do you feel—now? The anterior insula and human awareness. Nature Reviews Neuroscience, 10(1), 59–70.
Barrett, L. F. (2017). How Emotions Are Made: The Secret Life of the Brain. Houghton Mifflin Harcourt.
Kaplan, S. (1995). The restorative benefits of nature. Journal of Environmental Psychology, 15(3), 169–182.
design_implications: Restorative environments should provide sensory richness to facilitate interoceptive awareness; natural elements (water, vegetation) promote bodily awareness and recovery
High-demand environments should offer microrests aligned with fatigue and circadian rhythms; design spaces for brief restoration cycles
